body:
@jdm I think that this might actually be the behavior we expect based on what this issue describes? Since setting `e.width *= 2` doesn't update the image (maybe with srcset and lazy loading it could be different), we should expect a single `onload` event from when the image loads initially, then none from modifying the width.

That said, if we replace `e.width *= 2` with `e.sizes = "auto"` in the example, then chromium and safari send an endless stream of load events, whereas firefox sends two. In firefox it seems to only trigger when `e.sizes` is _changed_, rather than _set_, so one accounts for the load of the image, and the other is the initial set of `e.sizes`—I think this is the worst of both worlds.

Replacing `e.width *= 2` with `e.src = "https://joshmatthews.net/portrait.jpg"` gives endless streams of `onload` events in all three browsers, which is what we should expect from all these test cases according to the current spec, but not from this issue.

In any case, the spec probably needs to be updated here to clarify what the intended behavior is.
